3. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that the affidavit in support of the present petition has been filed on behalf of respondent No.2 which is placed at page 55 of the present petition.

4. According to the affidavit, the respondent No.2 has deposed that with the intervention friends and relatives, the matter between petitioner and himself have been amicably settled and also Anil Kumar & Ors vs State & Anr on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80645899/

sentences.text:
5. Respondent No.2 is present and reiterates the deposition contained in the affidavit dated 02.01.2023.
6.
In terms of the order passed by this Court, the IO has filed the updated status report under the cover of index dated 16.09.2023 through Ms. Nandita Rao, ASC.

A perusal of the status report,
particularly para 11 of the status report reveals that there is no sufficient evidence as of now to prosecute the present petitioner barring the allegation made by the complainant in this case.

For a better understanding, the contents of para 11 of the status report are extracted hereunder:-
"11.

That, as per Anand Swaroop Arora, after he was arrested by police in FIR No.
152/ 10, PS EOW and sent to JC, he remained in JC for 4-5 years till he got bail from the Ld. Court.

As per him, the alleged petitioners named herein in his absence, used to collect money under garb of Society and diverted those money for their own use and purchased properties from those funds which he cane to know only after he came out of jail and did personal enquiry, however he could not provide any material evidences to prove his oral allegations/assumptions.
There is no sufficient evidence enough on case file till now to prosecute the alleged petitioners except This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 26/09/2023 at 20:46:39 allegations made by the complainant of this case."

7. In view of above status report, which according to learned counsel appearing for the petitioner,
also reiterates the conclusion reached by the investigating authorities in their previous status report,
nothing survives for further adjudication since the investigating authorities themselves have not been able to bring out any material or substantive evidence to support the allegation levelled by the respondent No.2.

8. In view of lack of evidence, as revealed in the status report, and coupled with the settlement agreement having been arrived at between the petitioner and respondent No.2, this Court is of the considered opinion that no fruitful purpose would be served in continuing with the aforesaid FIR and the consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.

9. In view of the above, FIR No.438/2017 under Sections 420/403/34 IPC registered at Police Station Ambedkar Nagar, South- East, New Delhi and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are hereby quashed.
